prompt: A manager asks why a chatbot can state a wrong fact so fluently and confidently.
tells: state a wrong fact so fluently and confidently
why: Language models predict likely next tokens; that makes text fluent, not checked for truth.
trap: RAG is a fix; the question asks why it happens.

prompt: Watching a reply stream in word by word, a student asks how the model actually produces text.
tells: how the model actually produces text
why: The model repeatedly predicts the next token from everything before it.
trap: Streaming is how it's shown; next-token prediction is how it's made.

prompt: Which statement best describes how a large language model learned to write: memorizing a database of answers, or learning patterns from a huge amount of text?
tells: learning patterns from a huge amount of text
why: Pretraining teaches a model patterns of language by predicting the next token in huge amounts of text.
trap: Fine-tuning comes after pretraining and is much smaller.

prompt: A model doesn't know about a product released last month, even though it answers older questions well.
why: A model only knows patterns from its training data, which ends at a cutoff date.
trap: Settings don't add knowledge; grounding with current data would.

prompt: The word 'unbelievable' counts as three units toward the model's limit, not one.
why: Models read and write tokens, pieces of words. That's how text is split before prediction.
trap: Max tokens is the limit; tokenization explains what's being counted.

prompt: In 'The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big', the model must work out what 'it' refers to by weighing the other words.
why: The transformer's attention lets each token weigh every other token in the context to predict well.
trap: No multi-step reasoning model is needed; attention handles this in every language model.

prompt: Why can the same prompt give different answers on different runs, even with no changes to the model?
tells: even with no changes to the model
why: The model picks the next token by sampling from probabilities, so runs can differ (temperature controls how much).
trap: Nothing about the deployment changed; sampling is built into generation.

prompt: An image in a prompt is turned into pieces the model processes alongside the text tokens.
why: Multimodal models turn images and audio into tokens too, then predict as usual.
trap: OCR reads text from images; this is about how the model takes in any image.
